messages:
maria_support: FYI — customer reports sudden 429s hitting production around 12:04 UTC. They say it looks like minute-boundary spikes, but logs show bursts spread over ~20s. Pasting request trace and headers they captured.
maria_support: ```
REQUEST ID: req_ghx9
time: 2025-03-12T12:04:21Z
method: POST /v1/generate
client_ip: 3.122.45.11
x-ratelimit-mode: token
x-client-id: acme-ingest-42
headers: {
  "x-ratelimit-rpm": "1200",
  "x-ratelimit-tpm": "20000",
  "x-client-window-start": "2025-03-12T12:04:00Z",
  "x-client-window-end": "2025-03-12T12:05:00Z"
}
server-response: 429 Too Many Requests
server-headers: {
  "x-rate-limit-retry-after": "3",
  "x-rate-limit-rpm-used": "1198",
  "x-rate-limit-tpm-used": "19840"
}
```
maria_support: Customer says their SDK makes ~40 short streaming requests per minute per host and they're using short-lived keys rotated every 5m.
alan_sre: Good capture. Quick checks: are we seeing matching spikes in router/edge metrics? Can you paste the edge histogram for that minute (12:04)? Also ask customer for exact SDK version — streaming + many concurrent connects often multiplies token accounting.
chen_eng: Re: short-lived keys — rotation can cause fanout if clients re-acquire simultaneously. Also watch for concurrent HTTP/2 streams per connection. If each stream opens a new logical session we might double-count windows during token exchange.
maria_support: Attached edge tail below (filtered for client_id=acme-ingest-42) — looks like 430-460 reqs in a 20s window at 12:04:20-40. ```
[12:04:18.112] router: recv req req_ghw1
[12:04:18.189] router: recv req req_ghw2
[12:04:19.010] edge: connect from 3.122.45.11
[12:04:20.001] edge: batch_assign shard=7
[12:04:21.003] router: ratecap check -> allow but close to window
[12:04:21.384] backend: queue_len=0 exec=2
[12:04:22.000] router: responded 429 to req_ghx9
[12:04:25.112] router: recv req req_ghy1
```
alan_sre: That many in 20s -> RPM enforcement will spike. Two hypotheses: (1) client sending many parallel short requests that align with our minute window, (2) their token refill/rotation or retry loop causing synchronous bursts. Ask if they use exponential backoff or fixed sleep.
maria_support: Customer says they back off 1s fixed for 429s and retry up to 3 times (no jitter). They do a key rotation step that queries the auth endpoint then immediately resumes traffic.
chen_eng: Fixed 1s backoff + simultaneous rotation = classic stampede. Recommend they add jitter and increase initial backoff to 2s, plus stagger key rotation across hosts. Also from our side we can: a) enable soft-smoothing for this client for a day, b) suggest RATE_LIMIT headers debug config so they can see per-second allocation.
alan_sre: For immediate mitigation I can temporarily raise their per-minute soft cap from 1200->1800 on a short window to buy time while they patch client. But need approval for quota override (ops). maria_support can you confirm billing/security ok with temporary increase?
maria_support: Checking with billing now. Also asked them to switch to SDK version v2.4.1 which has jittered backoff. They replied they are on v2.3.7.
ratebot: Automatic note: client acme-ingest-42 has 5 quota override requests this month; last one on 2025-02-28.

maria_support: Billing gave conditional OK for a 1-hour soft bump limited to non-bursting endpoints. I'll request ephemeral config change. Can you draft the change set alan_sre?
alan_sre: Drafting: ```
PATCH /internal/quotas/acme-ingest-42
{ "soft_rpm": 1800, "duration": 3600, "reason": "customer 429 stampede mitigation pending client fix" }
```
chen_eng: Also add a router fallback rule to reduce aggressive retries: set `retry-window-smoothing=true` for that client so requests are spread across micro-windows when possible.
maria_support: I've sent the patch to ops and alerted customer to upgrade SDK and add jitter. They said they can roll in next 30 minutes.
alan_sre: Once patch is live I'll monitor the 12:04-12:06 window and post edge counts. If we still see >250 reqs/20s I'll consider enabling request-coalescing for that client (may affect latency slightly).
chen_eng: For follow-up: we should add a KB note about "short-lived-key rotation causing minute-boundary fanout" with recommended client-side patterns (stagger rotation, add jitter, prefer streaming multiplexing). I'll draft one.
maria_support: Thanks. Next steps for us:
- alan_sre: apply soft_rpm patch and monitor (ETA 5m)
- chen_eng: draft KB + router smoothing PR (ETA today)
- maria_support: confirm customer SDK upgrade and verify reduced retries (ETA 30m)
alan_sre: Patch applied at 1895000022. Monitoring now. Early telemetry: 12:04 window now shows ~120 reqs/20s (down from 430). Will report back in 5m.
maria_support: Customer confirmed they upgraded to v2.4.1 and added jitter; they report errors dropped to near-zero.
alan_sre: Follow-up (12:09): no further 429s from client during 12:05-12:08. I'm marking this as mitigated but leaving soft cap for 1 hour as planned. :white_check_mark:
maria_support: Great — closing once KB draft is up and ops confirms quota rollback schedule.
chen_eng: I'll post the KB in #docs when ready. Also adding a short test case to our integration suite to simulate key-rotation fanout.
maria_support: Thanks team :pray:
